Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood DPA - proposed telemetry & subprocessors redlines

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team circulated a redline to Redwood's standard DPA and flagged two items that need explicit guidance from product/security:

1) Telemetry exports: Section 4.3 adds a broad right for Greyhaven to request "runtime telemetry exports" including request/response metadata and sample outputs for troubleshooting and model monitoring. They want an export cadence and assurances around PII minimization.

2) Subprocessor transparency: Clause 6.2 asks Redwood to provide a list of runtime subprocessors and an agreement that new subprocessors will be disclosed 30 days prior to onboarding, or Greyhaven may object.

Redlines attached (Greyhaven_DPA_redline_v1.pdf). Our security team will need your product/security sign-off on feasible scope for telemetry and how we can surface subprocessor lists without breaking other customers' confidentiality.

Can we get a consolidated response and a mutual action plan by EOD Wednesday? Samir (cc) will coordinate contracting.

Thanks,
Priya Desai
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Greyhaven

Attachments: Greyhaven_DPA_redline_v1.pdf, subprocessor_list_requested.csv

Thanks for the ping. Quick assessment from Security:

Telemetry exports
- We can provide aggregated runtime metrics and prefix/KV cache hit rates without exposing request/response contents. For request/response samples, we can provide redacted snippets (PII/healthcare identifiers removed) but must limit sampling rate (max 10 samples/week) and ensure samples are encrypted in transit with access logging.
- Export cadence: monthly by default. For urgent investigations, a 72-hour expedited export can be requested with an approvals workflow (Security & CS sign-off).
- Operational notes: samples containing model outputs are sensitive; we will only include them if the customer provides an explicit justification and a minimal sample set. We should require an MSA addendum that limits reuse of samples to debugging/quality and prohibits training.

Subprocessor disclosure
- We can provide a sanitized snapshot of runtime subprocessors (name, country, function) quarterly. We cannot disclose contractual specifics or other customers' identities. New critical subprocessors (those with access to decrypted telemetry) can be disclosed 30 days prior with the option for Greyhaven to suspend onboarding for cause. Non-critical infra changes should be included in quarterly updates.

Deliverables I propose:
1) A short "Telemetry Export Playbook" (CSV template + fields, redaction rules, access control steps, SLA on turnaround).
2) A "Subprocessor Disclosure Snapshot" template (fields: vendor, role, region, access level).
3) Contract language to add to the DPA: limited-purpose clause for telemetry samples + requirement for Greyhaven to sign an additional confidentiality addendum.

I'll draft the playbook and templates. Jasmine, can you confirm feasibility of the sample export mechanics (encryption, sampling, redaction pipeline) and effort estimate? Lauren, once we have product/security statements, can you propose tight contract language that meets Greyhaven's ask while protecting our platform?

- Olga
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-summary-2028-06.xlsx

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood DPA - proposed telemetry & subprocessors redlines

Quick follow-ups after looking at engineering constraints:

- Export mechanics: we can extend our telemetry export job to include a "redacted payload_samples" table. Redaction rules will remove common PII patterns (emails, CCNs, SSNs) plus user-specified keys. That work is ~5 engineer-days to implement a configurable redaction pipeline and an export format (CSV + zipped JSON examples).
- Sampling: implement server-side sampling with deterministic seed per customer to avoid duplicate sensitive samples. Sampling at 10/week is trivial; increasing to >50/week will cost additional storage/retention and must be scoped as paid-for professional services.
- Access: exports will be placed in a secured S3 bucket behind signed URLs with 14-day expiry; we will log downloads to our audit trail. Providing direct access to raw KV caches or full request logs is not acceptable.

I will prepare a minimal export template and an engineering estimate. Requesting product trade-offs: do we want to offer 1) monthly redacted exports (default), 2) monthly + 72-hour expedited upon approval, or 3) subscription add-on for higher-frequency samples? Recommend default (1) + (2) for enterprise customers with a PS engagement.

Jasmine Liu
Staff Engineer, Observability

Priya — thanks for the redline and for the clear asks. Internal alignment complete; summary and proposed mutual action plan below. Please find attachments: Telemetry_Export_Playbook_v1.pdf (template) and Subprocessor_Snapshot_Template.csv.

Summary of what Redwood can commit to now:
- Telemetry exports: Monthly redacted telemetry export including aggregated metrics and up to 10 redacted request/response samples per month. Samples will be redacted via a deterministic pipeline that strips PII and user-configured keys. Exports delivered to a secure, access-logged S3 location. For urgent incident investigations, we will support a one-time 72-hour expedited export subject to security approvals.
- Subprocessor disclosure: Quarterly sanitized snapshot (vendor, role, region, access level). For new critical subprocessors (those with access to decrypted samples), Redwood will provide 30 days' notice and allow Greyhaven to raise objections; objections must be raised with specific cause and will enter a remediation discussion.
- Contract language: We propose adding a telemetry limited-use clause that prohibits Greyhaven from using exported samples to train external models or redistribute them. We also request a mutual NDA-addendum specific to export handling.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Greyhaven to confirm if monthly + 10 samples is sufficient or whether you need a paid higher-frequency tier (let us know by Wed EOD).
2) If OK, Lauren will propose redline language to insert into your DPA and Samir can coordinate signature path.
3) I will attach the playbook and subprocessor snapshot for review — if approved, Security/Engineering will deliver the first export within 30 days of signature.

If you want a call to walk through the playbook, happy to set one up later this week.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Telemetry_Export_Playbook_v1.pdf, Subprocessor_Snapshot_Template.csv

If you can send Lauren's draft by tomorrow morning, we'll aim to have legal's final redline back by end of week and schedule a short signature call next week.

Appreciate the rapid turnaround.

Best,
